This suggests that INCB-057643 may exert its effects by modulating the activity of Cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 1, which in turn influences the activity of the Sodium/Potassium Transporting ATPase subunits. The evidence supports a possible regulatory pathway involving the binding of Naloxone to the ATPase subunits, with INCB-057643 potentially acting as a modulator in this process. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism where INCB-057643 could influence the function of the Sodium/Potassium Transporting ATPase subunits through the regulation of Cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 1.
